text:
Renee: Customer reported duplicate end-of-stream tokens in our browser sample after flaky connectivity. UI shows a short truncated completion, then a second full one.
Omar: Which sample and which streaming path?
Vik (mobile-qa): The public chat demo using fetch+ReadableStream inside a WKWebView clone. Steps: send long prompt, quickly lock screen and unlock (~300-600ms). Repro ~70% on iOS 15 webview.
Kai: That pattern screams resume + replay with naive byte-appending parser. Are we parsing SSE comment metadata anywhere in the browser wrapper?
Renee: No, the demo drops comment lines and just accumulates decoded text chunks, splitting on "\n\n".
Omar: Two failure modes: (1) split UTF-8 sequences across chunks -> JSON.parse errors for partial deltas; (2) server replaying earlier seqs causes duplicate tokens when client appends bytes.
Vik (mobile-qa): I captured a run: server emitted `: token_resume=rm45 seq=301` before disconnect, after reconnect it replayed from seq=299 and some tokens were re-sent. The demo had already rendered seq 300.
Kai: Browser Node parity issue: Node SDK had an ack/resume handshake and de-dupe by seq; browser wrapper never implemented that.
Omar: Quick fixes: keep a byte-tail for TextDecoder streaming decode to avoid splitting codepoints; parse comment metadata lines like `: token_resume=... seq=...` and expose them to the demo; maintain small recentSeq cache and drop any incoming chunk whose seq is in cache.
Renee: Low-risk UX bandaid: ignore duplicate `[DONE]` for the same seq id so customers don't see flashing final tokens while we ship full fix.
Vik (mobile-qa): I can automate the background/foreground timing with remote debug and produce a HAR + raw byte dump for failing runs.
Kai: Add a feature flag `enableSseSeqHandling` set false by default. With it on we do strict dedupe and emit `sse_seq_gap` telemetry if seq rewinds. With it off we do the duplicate-[DONE] guard only.
Omar: Tests needed: unit for decode tail behavior, unit for seq dedupe logic, integration that injects overlapping replay with duplicate final tokens to ensure single completion render. Add an e2e on BrowserStack/iOS to validate WKWebView timing.
Renee: Also update sample README with a short note about seq/resume semantics and how to enable the flag. Many customers copy-paste this code.
Kai: I'll open a small PR that: (1) plumbs comment-parsing into the browser fetch-stream parser; (2) keeps a byte tail across reads; (3) adds a bounded seenSeq window (512 entries) and a simple dedupe rule. Behind the flag.
Vik (mobile-qa): Once canary is up I'll run the harness across iOS 13-16 and Android webview and attach logs: connection lifecycle, parsed seqs, and raw bytes.
sdk-ci: Canary build scheduled: browser-sdk@0.23.0-canary to staging at 04:00 UTC.
Renee: Thanks team. This should improve parity with the Node SDK and reduce onboarding friction for mobile web demos.
